reference_answer:
The polynomial split is f_e(x)=(f(x)+f(-x))/2 and f_o(x)=(f(x)-f(-x))/2. Direct substitution shows f_e is even, f_o is odd, and f_e+f_o=f. If f=e+o with e even and o odd, then f(-x)=e(x)-o(x), so adding/subtracting recovers these same formulas; uniqueness is as polynomials, not a claim that their evaluations on one spectrum uniquely determine them.

For the finite-dimensional Hermitian operator in the quantum circuit setting, write A=V diag(lambda_i)V†. An even polynomial's right singular-value transform equals its eigenvalue function because f_e(|lambda|)=f_e(lambda); an odd polynomial's balanced transform supplies the sign of lambda, giving f_o(lambda). Choose any unitary sign completion at zero eigenvalues; f_o(0)=0 makes that choice immaterial. Hence the parity-respecting construction implements the desired two functions, not an arbitrary mixed-parity singular-value function of a non-Hermitian matrix.

Input access and scale are real obligations. If A is not already given as an exact normalized block, choose a known rho>0 with ||A||<=rho and let B=A/rho. Obtain an exact block encoding of B and use the definite-parity polynomials g_e(x)=f_e(rho*x) and g_o(x)=f_o(rho*x). They retain their parities and g_e(B)=f_e(A), g_o(B)=f_o(A). A finite Hermitian matrix has such a rho. Concretely, for S=sqrt(I-B^2), the block matrix U_B=[[B,S],[S,-B]] is unitary: spectral functional calculus gives BS=SB and B^2+S^2=I, so its square is I and its clean block is B. Expanding each g in its finite definite-parity Chebyshev basis, implementing the corresponding qubitized blocks, and using phase-aware coefficient LCU gives each parity branch at a positive coefficient-norm factor (with a separate zero-block construction when necessary). This is existence/construction mathematics, not an efficient oracle-synthesis guarantee from the word Hermitian alone. Chebyshev coefficients, coefficient preparation, SELECT and input-oracle work must actually be supplied and charged in any implementation; approximation would require an additional error contract. Nothing here assumes ||A||<=1 without this normalization step.

Put E=f_e(A) and O=f_o(A). Implement the two parity branches at compatible clean signal registers s and a common positive scale c, meaning J†U_e J=E/c and J†U_o J=O/c with J|psi>=|0^r>_s|psi>. The scale need not be minimal. Workspace padding preserves a clean block. If existing nonzero-branch factors are c_e,c_o, take c>=max(c_e,c_o) and explicitly attenuate their accepted blocks by c_e/c or c_o/c, for example by a clean-qubit rotation whose00 matrix element is that ratio. Its clean register is included in s before combining; equalization/padding is not free and is not part of the assertion that the COMBINER adds just one qubit. A zero branch can be represented by a unitary with zero accepted block, for instance X on a signal qubit, at any chosen positive c; never divide by its zero coefficient norm.

Introduce exactly one new selector b and set SELECT=|0><0|_b tensor U_e+|1><1|_b tensor U_o, with V=(H_b tensor I)SELECT(H_b tensor I). For every normalized input |psi>, the complete projected-port transcript is
V|0>_b|0^r>_s|psi>
 = |0>_b|0^r>_s (E+O)|psi>/(2c)
 + |1>_b|0^r>_s (E-O)|psi>/(2c) + |G_psi>,
where (I_b tensor <0^r|_s tensor I)|G_psi>=0. Thus projection onto the FIXED b=0,s=0 port gives f(A)/(2c), a block encoding with declared factor2c. It is a projected block, not an assertion that the full unitary output has no garbage. Its success probability is ||f(A)psi||^2/(4c^2); if f(A)psi=0 it is0 and there is no normalized conditional output. Otherwise conditioning on this port gives f(A)psi/||f(A)psi||, with the exact coherent phase retained.

The coefficient1/2 is forced by this particular balanced H-SELECT-H and this chosen projector: each branch contributes the product of two Hadamard entries1/sqrt(2). It cannot be changed while leaving those operations and that accepted port fixed. This is the precise sense of unavoidable in the naive combination. It is not a universal lower bound on block factors or a state-independent claim about probability loss. The alternative control port contains (E-O)/(2c), not generically the sum, but it need not be useless or distinct on every allowed spectrum. For f(x)=1+x and A=0, a genuinely parity-mixed polynomial has E=I,O=0, and BOTH signal-clean control ports carry I/(2c). For E=0 they differ only by a minus sign. Conversely E=O gives a zero difference port. Polynomial parity alone does not preclude any of these operator degeneracies.

Other schemes can use different accepted projectors, exploit known zero/equal branches, or use coefficient-weighted LCU: factors c_e,c_o give sum factor c_e+c_o using amplitudes sqrt(c_e/(c_e+c_o)) and sqrt(c_o/(c_e+c_o)), rather than2*max(c_e,c_o). That comparison does not remove the literal1/2 from the fixed common-c balanced selected block. A claimed minimal normalization or a complete gate, input-preparation, postselection/amplification or readout complexity theorem would require separate analysis.

rubric.criterion: Derives and proves uniqueness of the polynomial even/odd split, distinguishing polynomial uniqueness from degeneracies after evaluating on spec(A).

Explains why definite-parity SVT gives the corresponding eigenvalue function for Hermitian A, including null eigenvalues; makes any A/rho input normalization, polynomial rescaling and oracle/preparation/equalization work explicit rather than silently assuming a unit-normalized available input.

Uses compatible clean signal registers and common c>0 to calculate H-SELECT-H: chosen b0,s0 block f(A)/(2c), other clean control block (f_e(A)-f_o(A))/(2c), flag-orthogonal garbage and the actual input-dependent success probability/zero-output boundary.

Explains the forced1/2 only for this fixed balanced common-c selected-port scheme. Refutes exclusive-success-port/global-optimality overclaims with an allowed degenerate-spectrum example and separates weighted LCU, workspace equalization, implementation and amplification costs.

exposition.core_summary: The unique parity split combines into the fixed all-zero balanced block f(A)/(2c); the other control port is the difference and can coincide with the sum on degenerate spectra. The factor2 is a fixed-scheme accounting identity, not exclusive success or universal optimality.

semantic_steps.claim: The parity averages are even/odd polynomials, sum to f, and are uniquely recovered by adding/subtracting f(x) and f(-x).
Definite-parity transforms equal the desired functions of Hermitian A, with input normalization/rescaling and compatible common-c branch encodings made explicit.
A new balanced selector controls the two completed parity encodings on the same signal workspace.
After recombination, the clean b0 port is (E+O)/(2c), the clean b1 port is (E-O)/(2c), and remaining terms are orthogonal to the clean signal subspace.
The fixed chosen block is f(A)/(2c) with input-dependent success probability; zero target output cannot be normalized conditionally.
The1/2 follows from fixed Hadamard matrix elements, not exclusive-success-port or global optimality; allowed degenerate spectra and alternative weighted schemes delimit the claim.
